the “conflict” is a false one, as the IRB members are not in a position to influence the protocol, but the “conflict-of-interest” is real, as it is an impediment to the IRB members being able to provide a complete and unbiased review of the protocol.

IRB deliberations should be inclusive, not exclusive, and the process of disclosure and evaluation of conflicts of interest should not be used as a means to silence the most knowledgeable members of an IRB.

“conflict of interest” is a term that is often misunderstood and misused, that the term is often misapplied to individuals who have no actual conflict and who may be the most qualified and knowledgeable to participate in the deliberative process, that exclusion of individuals with actual conflicts may have undesirable consequences, and that IRBs should be cautious about excluding individuals with perceived conflicts from the deliberative processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IRB should be the arbiter of whether a conflict of interest exists, and that the IRB has the responsibility to manage such a conflict.
, while the potential for bias is real, it is also possible that the most appropriate individuals to serve on an IRB may be the very ones with a “conflict of interest.”
IRB members should be allowed and encouraged to participate in IRB deliberations, even in the presence of potential or perceived conflicts of interest.
